successCriteria.description: The App router defines exactly four routes — /login (public) and /, /leaves, /leaves/:id (guarded) — and wraps them in AuthProvider; navigating to any guarded route while the session is null redirects to /login.

RequireAuth is the single code path for the unauthenticated→/login redirect: it reads useAuth() and, when session is null, renders a replace-navigation to /login; no page or component implements its own 401/redirect logic.

LoginPage: on successful login it navigates to the dashboard; on failure it renders the server's error message verbatim and never distinguishes wrong-email from wrong-password (no email-existence hint).
DashboardPage renders the signed-in employee from EmployeeService.getMe and their balances from BalanceService.getBalances.
LeaveListPage renders LeaveService.list() rows each showing leave type, dates, and status; LeaveDetailPage renders LeaveService.getById(id) using the :id route param.
Every view that renders a date imports formatUtcDate from web/src/shared/date/index.ts; no list/detail view defines its own date formatter or uses bare local Date getters/string-slicing.

Vitest component tests exist for the login flow (success routes to dashboard; failure shows the server message without email-existence hints) and for the 401/unauthenticated redirect-to-login behaviour.

constraints: No UI component library and no state-management library — presentation state is React state/context only.

The presentation layer must not import from any module's internals — only from public entry points (web/src/modules/auth/index.ts, web/src/modules/employee/index.ts, web/src/modules/leave/index.ts, web/src/shared/date/index.ts, web/src/shared/types/index.ts).
The frontend is read-only for leave requests: no create/submit/approve/reject/cancel UI or calls are introduced.
AuthProvider's existing constructor contract (authService, tokenStorage, apiClient props) is consumed as-is; the presentation layer must not re-implement login/logout/token handling.
No files under src/ (the Fastify backend) are modified; the backend build and its tests remain untouched.
outOfScope: Any leave-request state transition (create/submit/approve/reject/cancel) UI or API calls — the frontend is read-only.
Role-gated or manager/HR-admin screens — no role-based view switching beyond the single authenticated guard.
Proactive JWT expiry detection — expiry is detected solely via the server's 401 (already handled by the API client).
README documentation and the broader component-test suite (Phase 6).

entityInvariants.invariant: The anonymous state is represented by a null session everywhere (context value, guard check); an authenticated session always carries token + profile + status AUTHENTICATED. The presentation layer never constructs a session object itself — it only reads useAuth().session.
Rendered read-only; status is display-only and never mutated by the frontend. All date fields (startDate, endDate, submittedAt, decidedAt, cancelledAt) render through formatUtcDate.
Rendered read-only; available is display-only and never recomputed or mutated by the frontend. periodStart/periodEnd render through formatUtcDate.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Renders children only when useAuth().session is non-null; otherwise performs a replace-navigation to /login. This is the sole redirect-to-login code path.
Public (no session required). On success navigates to the dashboard; on failure surfaces the server error message verbatim with no email-existence distinction.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Login failure renders the ApiError message as-is; wrong-email and wrong-password are indistinguishable.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Calls useAuth().logout() and returns the user to the login screen.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Every date-rendering view imports formatUtcDate (and parseUtcDate where needed) from the shared date module — never a local formatter, bare local Date getters, or ISO string-slicing.
The presentation layer consumes the auth session via useAuth()/AuthProvider and must match the existing anonymous-as-null contract and the AuthProvider props (authService, tokenStorage, apiClient).

Pages consume the read-only service interfaces (IEmployeeService.getMe, ILeaveService.list/getById, IBalanceService.getBalances) exactly as exported — no new service methods or direct API-client calls in the presentation layer.

All entity shapes (EmployeeProfile, LeaveRequestView, LeaveBalanceView, LeaveStatus, LeaveTypeCode, AuthSessionStatus) are imported from the shared types module and never re-declared or extended in the presentation layer.

integrationPoints.why: The router wraps routes in AuthProvider and the guard/pages read the session via useAuth(); login/logout flow is delegated to the auth module.
DashboardPage renders the signed-in employee via getMe.
LeaveListPage/LeaveDetailPage render requests via list/getById; DashboardPage renders balances via getBalances.
All date rendering in list/detail/dashboard views goes through the single shared UTC formatter.
Pages type their rendered data against the canonical shared types.
